title: Does the strip overlap itself after a half turn?
description: The trapezium strip is turned by one hundred and eighty degrees about its centre dot. The shorter side goes to the bottom and the longer side to the top, so the turned strip does not overlap the original. Keeko's doubt is that it does overlap, because the slanting sides swap.
teaching_notes: One idea: a half turn swaps the top and bottom sides, and when they are different in length the turned strip cannot overlap the original. Watch for students who check only the sides that are equal.

source: After the strip is rotated by 180� about its centre, does it
video_script.why: The child sees that a half turn swaps the shorter top side with the longer bottom side, so the turned strip cannot lie exactly on the original.
video_script.substitution: Turn the strip by a half turn and compare its top and bottom sides with the start picture.
video_script.anchor: a strip shaped like a trapezium, shorter on top and longer at the bottom, with equal slanting sides and a dot at its centre
video_script.wrong_answer: yes, it overlaps, because the slanting sides swap
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says yes, it overlaps, because the slanting sides swap. The slanting sides are equal, so they do fit, but the shorter side goes to the bottom where the original has the longer side, so a gap is left.
video_script.payoff_line: The turned strip does not fit the original

final_answer.value: No. After 180 degrees the shorter side is at the bottom and the longer side at the top, so it does not fit the original
final_answer.spoken: the turned strip does not fit the original

maths_rules: Two pictures overlap when one lies exactly on the other, with no part sticking out
A half turn is a turn of 180 degrees about the centre; it swaps the top of a shape with its bottom
The top side of the strip is shorter than its bottom side, so after a half turn the shorter side is at the bottom and the longer side is on top
The slanting sides are equal, so they swap and fit, but the top and bottom sides do not, so the turned strip does not overlap the original
video_script.design: One idea: a half turn swaps the shorter top side with the longer bottom side, so the strip cannot overlap itself. The strip stays on the board all video. Wrong idea: the slanting sides swap, so it overlaps.
